highlights.description: Security release: secrets are redacted when formatted or logged, and the file provider keeps secret paths inside its directory and refuses secret files other users can read. Adds a SQL table-backed provider (`sql://`). `Secret.String` is removed in favour of `Secret.Reveal`

breaking.description: `vault.Secret.String` is removed. Formatting a `Secret` or `*Secret` with `fmt` (any verb) or logging it with `log/slog` now prints `[REDACTED]`; read the value with `Secret.Reveal` (or `Secret.Bytes`)
File provider: a secret path that is empty, absolute or leaves the directory with `..` fails with `vault.ErrInvalidPath`, and a symbolic link resolving outside the directory is refused
File provider: `Get` returns an error matching `file.ErrInsecurePermissions` for a secret file that group or others can access, unless `Config.AllowInsecurePermissions` is set

upgradeGuide.description: Replace every `secret.String()` call with `secret.Reveal()`; the compiler finds these

Search for code that obtains the value by formatting a secret, such as `fmt.Sprintf("%s", secret)` or `fmt.Sprint(secret)`, and use `secret.Reveal()` instead; these still compile but now yield `[REDACTED]`

File provider: make secret files private (`chmod 600`); for a mounted volume you cannot change, set `defaultMode: 0600` or, if access is restricted another way, `file.Config{AllowInsecurePermissions: true}`
File provider: use secret paths relative to `Directory`, without `..` segments or absolute paths, and replace symbolic links that point outside the directory with the files themselves
Build with Go 1.26 or later, then run `go get github.com/plexusone/omnivault@v0.6.0` and `go mod tidy`

security.description: `Secret.String` returned the plaintext value, so passing a secret to `fmt`, wrapping it into an error with `%v`, or logging it with `log/slog` wrote the value into logs; formatting a `Secret` value (not a pointer) also printed its `Value` and `Fields`. `GoString`, `Format` and `LogValue` now produce `[REDACTED]` (`vault.Redacted`) for `Secret` and `*Secret`, for every `fmt` verb and for `log/slog`. JSON encoding is unchanged, since providers use it to store and transfer secrets

The file provider joined the secret path onto its directory without checking the result, so a path such as `../other/secret` read, wrote or deleted files outside the directory, and a symbolic link inside the directory could point anywhere. Secret paths must now be local, and files are opened through `os.Root`, which also refuses symbolic links that resolve outside the directory

The file provider wrote secret files with a private mode but read any file regardless of its mode, so a group- or world-readable secret was accepted silently. `Get` now checks the mode of the opened file; platforms that do not enforce file modes are unaffected

added.description: `Secret.Reveal` returns the primary value (`ValueBytes` as a string if set, otherwise `Value`), and `vault.Redacted` is the marker a secret prints as
`file.Config.AllowInsecurePermissions` and `file.ErrInsecurePermissions`

SQL table-backed provider (`providers/sqlstore`) storing AES-GCM encrypted secrets in an application-owned table, for MySQL-compatible databases (including Dolt), PostgreSQL and SQLite, with optional auto-migration and read-only mode
`ProviderSQL` and the `SQLConfig` alias, so `sql://` URIs resolve through the same config-based provider dispatch as the other built-in providers

changed.description: Bump `github.com/grokify/oscompat` from 0.3.0 to 0.9.0, which provides the private-permission check the file provider uses
`sqlstore`: drop an unused placeholder index parameter

documentation.description: README documents the `sql://` SQL store provider
Provider guide documents the file provider's path and permission rules and uses the `Directory` config field
Client and quickstart guides read secrets with `Reveal`

tests.description: Tests for secret redaction across `fmt` verbs and `log/slog`, and for path containment and permission checks in the file provider
